newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares finish lower, some profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares finish lower, some profit-taking.

text.p: Norwegian shares traded in negative territory amid profit-taking in some blue-chip stock on Wednesday, dealers said.
Oslo's Total share index closed 0.21 percent lower at 1,056.30 points. Turnover was moderate at 962 million crowns.
"We continued to be affected by Wall Street," one dealer said. "Blue chips fell and we saw some profit-taking, especially in Orkla which has performed well lately. Otherwise it was a dull day."

Orkla, a food-based conglomerate, saw its A share slip 1.9 percent to 500 crowns the day after beverage group Coca Cola said it had agreed to end cooperation with Nordic drinks company Pripps Ringnes AB, which is a joint venture of Orkla and Swedish vehicle maker Volvo AB.

Saga Petroleum said on Wednesday it had started up the Vigdis oilfield in the Norwegian North Sea five months ahead of schedule and 600 million crowns under budget. But its A share shed 1.6 percent to close at 122.50 crowns.
"Saga Petroleum is a good buy on this level," one dealer said.
